news.title: Spain vs England player ratings —Tuchel’s men stun EURO and World Cup winner in Madrid
news.lede: Madrid World Cup winner Spain was beaten for the first time in more than two years after losing 2-3 at home to England in the Nations League on Sunday. Spain’s 43-game unbeaten streak ended with a first defeat since a 0-1 loss to Colombia in March 2024 in a friendly match played at Wembley Stadium in London. La Roja Furia were constantly troubled by World Cup semifinalist England’s intense pressing game. England’s goals came via a penalty from captain Harry Kane — who grabbed his 93rd goal for England — and defenders Ezri Konsa and Ben White.

news.title: England didn't repeat World Cup mistake, taking forward step
news.lede: England beat Spain 3-2 in Madrid to top their UEFA Nations League group, despite Elliot Anderson being sent off with a red card during the win. England took a step in the right direction as they came into their game against Spain, having not beaten the world's number-one team since the FIFA rankings were introduced in 1992. After losing 3-2 to Spain at Wembley and failing to beat Argentina in the World Cup, the game against Spain in Madrid was about England rectifying both defeats and proving they could do the job against another elite nation. Having already booked a place in the UEFA Nations League quarter-finals anyway, this game was about whether they had learned from their mistakes and whether there was any truth to the idea that they could close the gap.

news.title: Spain 2-3 England talking points: Thomas Tuchel learns lessons from Argentina as Harry Kane, Ben White and Lewis Hall shine
news.lede: After England beat Spain in their own back yard in a statement result, we look at the main talking points from a memorable moment in Madrid... Bold England show their strengths with front-foot approach England's football DNA has been in focus this autumn. In Madrid, we saw the English style at its best. From the first whistle, England were boldly on the front foot, overwhelming Spain with pace, power and directness.

news.title: Spain 2-3 England: Three Lions produce best win under Thomas Tuchel
news.lede: Harry Kane scored for a record-equalling seventh England away game. Thomas Tuchel went with bold words when reminded about the caution that sabotaged England's World Cup hopes and left them with so much to prove against Spain in the Nations League on Sunday. In a media theatre at the Metropolitano in Madrid, head coach Tuchel's sixth sense led him to go public with what he was convinced England would produce against the world champions. Tuchel looked his inquisitors in the eyes and declared: "We are up for something spectacular."

news.title: England fans taunt world champs after World Cup trophy flex
news.lede: Updated November 16, 2026 - 12.08am. First published November 15, 2026 - 10.46pm. England fans chanted “are you Scotland in disguise” as Thomas Tuchel’s men ended Spain’s remarkable 43-game unbeaten run with a 3-2 Nations League upset in Madrid on Monday (AEDT). England led 3-0 after 57 minutes as Harry Kane, Ezri Konsa and Ben White found the back of the net at the Metropolitano Stadium.

news.title: Boycotts, bans and no-shows: Notable World Cup absentees
news.lede: The first World Cup was hosted by Uruguay in 1930 and featured 13 teams, just four of which were from Europe: France, Belgium, Romania and Yugoslavia. The paucity of European teams wasn't due to a boycott but largely had to do with funds being short during the Great Depression and the difficulty of traveling such a long distance by sea. It would be linked to a boycott at the next World Cup. Italy both hosted and won their first World Cup in 1934.
